name: London
blurb: London has hundreds of masjids, and most hold Jumma shortly after midday. Larger masjids in areas like East London, Tooting and Harrow often run two or three Jummah congregations to manage the crowds.
tip: Central London masjids fill up fast — aim to arrive 20–30 minutes before the khutbah.

name: Birmingham
blurb: Birmingham has one of the largest Muslim communities in the UK, with masjids across Small Heath, Sparkbrook and Aston. Jumma is typically held just after Dhuhr, with times shifting through the year.
tip: Many Birmingham masjids hold a second Jummah — check both times in the app before you set out.

name: Manchester
blurb: Greater Manchester has masjids spread across Rusholme, Cheetham Hill, Longsight and beyond. Most hold a single Jumma congregation shortly after midday.
tip: If you're near the universities, several masjids run a campus-friendly early Jummah.

name: New York City
blurb: New York City has masjids in every borough, from Manhattan to Astoria, the Bronx and Brooklyn. Many city-centre masjids run multiple Jummah sessions to fit working crowds.
masjids: Islamic Cultural Center of New York
tip: Midtown masjids may hold 1:00 PM and 2:00 PM Jummah sessions — pick whichever fits your schedule.

name: Chicago
blurb: Chicago and its suburbs — Bridgeview, Rogers Park, Villa Park — have a long-established Muslim community with many masjids holding Jumma just after midday.
tip: The Downtown Islamic Center is convenient if you're working or visiting the Loop on a Friday.

name: Houston
blurb: Houston has one of the fastest-growing Muslim populations in the US, with large masjids across Southwest Houston, Sugar Land and Katy. Many run multiple Jummah congregations.
tip: Houston's larger Islamic centres often hold three Jummah sessions — the app shows each start time.

name: Los Angeles
blurb: Greater Los Angeles has masjids spread from the Westside to the San Gabriel Valley and Orange County. Jumma is generally held shortly after midday.
tip: LA traffic is unpredictable on Fridays — set a reminder and leave early.

name: Toronto
blurb: The Greater Toronto Area has masjids across Scarborough, Mississauga, North York and downtown. Many hold two or more Jummah congregations.
tip: Downtown Toronto offices often have a nearby musalla — but full Jumma with khutbah is at the masjids listed in the app.

name: Dubai
blurb: Dubai has masjids in nearly every neighbourhood, and Jumma times are closely tied to the official Dhuhr time, which shifts through the year.
masjids: Al Farooq Omar Bin Al Khattab Mosque
tip: In Dubai the Jumma khutbah usually begins very close to the official Dhuhr time — check the exact minute in the app.

name: Sydney
blurb: Sydney's masjids are concentrated in the west and south-west — Lakemba, Auburn, Bankstown — with others across the city. Most hold Jumma shortly after midday.
tip: Lakemba Mosque is one of the largest in the Southern Hemisphere — arrive early on Fridays.

name: Singapore
blurb: Singapore's mosques are managed with MUIS oversight, and Jumma (Jumaat) is held across the island shortly after midday, often with two sessions at busier mosques.
tip: City-centre mosques like Masjid Al-Falah are convenient if you're working near Orchard Road.

name: Kuala Lumpur
blurb: Kuala Lumpur has masjids throughout the city, and Jumma (Jumaat) is held shortly after midday. Larger masjids draw big congregations on Fridays.
tip: Masjid Jamek is central and easy to reach by LRT if you're travelling through KL on a Friday.
